segs.e: Numbered Discourses 7.1
1. Wealth
Pleasing (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lābhakāmo ca hoti, sakkārakāmo ca hoti, anavaññattikāmo ca hoti, ahiriko ca hoti, anottappī ca, pāpiccho ca, micchādiṭṭhi ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant desires material things, honor, and status. They lack conscience and prudence. They have corrupt wishes and wrong view.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with these seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti, manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lābhakāmo ca hoti, na sakkārakāmo ca hoti, na anavaññattikāmo ca hoti, hirīmā ca hoti, ottappī ca, appiccho ca, sammādiṭṭhi ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t desire material things, honor, and status. They have conscience and prudence. They have few desires and right view.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 7.2
1. Wealth
Pleasing (2nd)

segs.p: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lābhakāmo ca hoti, sakkārakāmo ca hoti, anavaññattikāmo ca hoti, ahiriko ca hoti, anottappī ca, issukī ca, maccharī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant desires material things, honor, and status. They lack conscience and prudence. They’re jealous and stingy.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with these seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lābhakāmo ca hoti, na sakkārakāmo ca hoti, na anavaññattikāmo ca hoti, hirīmā ca hoti, ottappī ca, anissukī ca, amaccharī ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t desire material things, honor, and status. They have conscience and prudence. They’re not jealous or stingy.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 7.3
1. Wealth
Powers in Brief
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme …pe…
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. …
“Mendicants, there are these seven powers.
What seven?

segs.p: Saddhābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, hirībalaṁ, ottappabalaṁ, satibalaṁ, samādhibalaṁ, paññābalaṁ.
segs.e: The powers of faith, energy, conscience, prudence, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.
These are the seven powers.
The powers are faith and energy,
conscience and prudence,
mindfulness and immersion,
and wisdom as the seventh power.
Empowered by these,
an astute mendicant lives happily.
They should examine the teaching rationally,
discerning the meaning with wisdom.
The liberation of their heart
is like a lamp going out.”
Numbered Discourses 7.4
1. Wealth
Powers in Detail
“Mendicants, there are these seven powers.
What seven?

segs.p: Saddhābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, hirībalaṁ, ottappabalaṁ, satibalaṁ, samādhibalaṁ, paññābalaṁ.
segs.e: The powers of faith, energy, conscience, prudence, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.
And what is the power of faith?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
This is called the power of faith.
And what is the power of energy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.
This is called the power of energy.
And what is the power of conscience?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako hirīmā hoti, hirīyati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, hirīyati pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has a conscience. They’re conscientious about bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and conscientious about acquiring any bad, unskillful qualities.
This is called the power of conscience.
And what is the power of prudence?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ottappī hoti, ottappati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, ottappati pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is prudent. They’re prudent when it comes to bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and prudent when it comes to the acquiring of any bad, unskillful qualities.
This is called the power of prudence.
And what is the power of mindfulness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.
This is called the power of mindfulness.
And what is the power of immersion?

It’s when a noble disciple, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected. …

With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.
This is called the power of immersion.
And what is the power of wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
This is called the power of wisdom.
These are the seven powers.
The powers are faith and energy,
conscience and prudence,
mindfulness and immersion,
and wisdom as the seventh power.
Empowered by these,
an astute mendicant lives happily.
They should examine the teaching rationally,
discerning the meaning with wisdom.
The liberation of their heart
is like a lamp going out.”
Numbered Discourses 7.5
1. Wealth
Wealth in Brief
“Mendicants, there are these seven kinds of wealth.
What seven?

segs.p: Saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hirīdhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.
segs.e: The wealth of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
These are the seven kinds of wealth.
Faith and ethical conduct are kinds of wealth,
as are conscience and prudence,
learning and generosity,
and wisdom is the seventh kind of wealth.
When a woman or man
has these kinds of wealth,
they’re said to be prosperous,
their life is not in vain.
So let the wise devote themselves
to faith, ethical behavior,
confidence, and insight into the teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”
Numbered Discourses 7.6
1. Wealth
Wealth in Detail
“Mendicants, there are these seven kinds of wealth.
What seven?

segs.p: Saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hirīdhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.
segs.e: The wealth of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
And what is the wealth of faith?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening …

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho …pe… buddho bhagavā’ti.

segs.e: This is called the wealth of faith.
And what is the wealth of ethical conduct?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
This is called the wealth of ethical conduct.
And what is the wealth of conscience?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako hirīmā hoti, hirīyati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, hirīyati pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has a conscience. They’re conscientious about bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and conscientious about having any bad, unskillful qualities.
This is called the wealth of conscience.
And what is the wealth of prudence?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ottappī hoti, ottappati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, ottappati pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is prudent. They’re prudent when it comes to bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and prudent when it comes to the acquiring of any bad, unskillful qualities.
This is called the wealth of prudence.
And what is the wealth of learning?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti. Tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
This is called the wealth of learning.
And what is the wealth of generosity?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.
This is called the wealth of generosity.
And what is the wealth of wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti …pe… sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
This is called the wealth of wisdom.
These are the seven kinds of wealth.
Faith and ethical conduct are kinds of wealth,
as are conscience and prudence,
learning and generosity,
and wisdom is the seventh kind of wealth.
When a woman or man
has these kinds of wealth,
they’re said to be prosperous,
their life is not in vain.
So let the wise devote themselves
to faith, ethical behavior,
confidence, and insight into the teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”
Numbered Discourses 7.7
1. Wealth
With Ugga

segs.p: Atha kho uggo rājamahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho uggo rājamahāmatto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ugga the government chief minister went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāva aḍḍho cāyaṁ, bhante, migāro rohaṇeyyo yāva mahaddhano yāva mahābhogo”ti.
segs.e: Migāra of Rohaṇa is so rich, so very wealthy.”

segs.p: “Kīva aḍḍho panugga, migāro rohaṇeyyo, kīva mahaddhano, kīva mahābhogo”ti?
segs.e: “But Ugga, how rich is he?”

segs.p: “Sataṁ, bhante, satasahassānaṁ hiraññassa, ko pana vādo rūpiyassā”ti.
segs.e: “He has a hundred thousand gold coins, not to mention the silver coins!”

segs.p: “Atthi kho etaṁ, ugga, dhanaṁ netaṁ ‘natthī’ti vadāmīti.
segs.e: “Well, Ugga, that is wealth, I can’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, ugga, dhanaṁ sādhāraṇaṁ agginā udakena rājūhi corehi appiyehi dāyādehi.
segs.e: But fire, water, rulers, thieves, and unloved heirs all take a share of that wealth.

segs.p: Satta kho imāni, ugga, dhanāni asādhāraṇāni agginā udakena rājūhi corehi appiyehi dāyādehi.
segs.e: There are these seven kinds of wealth that they can’t take a share of.
What seven?

segs.p: Saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hirīdhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.
segs.e: The wealth of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

segs.p: Imāni kho, ugga, satta dhanāni asādhāraṇāni agginā udakena rājūhi corehi appiyehi dāyādehīti.
segs.e: There are these seven kinds of wealth that fire, water, rulers, thieves, and unloved heirs can’t take a share of.
Faith and ethical conduct are kinds of wealth,
as are conscience and prudence,
learning and generosity,
and wisdom is the seventh kind of wealth.
When a woman or man
has these kinds of wealth,
they’re really rich in the world,
invincible among gods and humans.
So let the wise devote themselves
to faith, ethical behavior,
confidence, and insight into the teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”
Numbered Discourses 7.8
1. Wealth
Fetters
“Mendicants, there are these seven fetters.
What seven?

segs.p: Anunayasaṁyojanaṁ, paṭighasaṁyojanaṁ, diṭṭhisaṁyojanaṁ, vicikicchāsaṁyojanaṁ, mānasaṁyojanaṁ, bhavarāgasaṁyojanaṁ, avijjāsaṁyojanaṁ.
segs.e: The fetters of attraction, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.
These are the seven fetters.”
Numbered Discourses 7.9
1. Wealth
Giving Up

segs.p: “Sattannaṁ, bhikkhave, saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these seven fetters.
What seven?

segs.p: Anunayasaṁyojanassa pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati, paṭighasaṁyojanassa …pe…
segs.e: The fetters of attraction, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sattannaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: The spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these seven fetters.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno anunayasaṁyojanaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
segs.e: When a mendicant has given up the fetters of attraction, repulsion, views, doubt, conceit, desire to be reborn, and ignorance—cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future—

segs.p: avijjāsaṁyojanaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”ti.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”
Numbered Discourses 7.10
1. Wealth
Stinginess
“Mendicants, there are these seven fetters.
What seven?

segs.p: Anunayasaṁyojanaṁ, paṭighasaṁyojanaṁ, diṭṭhisaṁyojanaṁ, vicikicchāsaṁyojanaṁ, mānasaṁyojanaṁ, issāsaṁyojanaṁ, macchariyasaṁyojanaṁ.
segs.e: The fetters of attraction, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, jealousy, and stinginess.
These are the seven fetters.”
Numbered Discourses 7.11
2. Tendencies
Underlying Tendencies (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these seven underlying tendencies.
What seven?

segs.p: Kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo.
segs.e: The underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.
These are the seven underlying tendencies.”
Numbered Discourses 7.12
2. Tendencies
Underlying Tendencies (2nd)

segs.p: “Sattannaṁ, bhikkhave, anusayānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these seven underlying tendencies.
What seven?

segs.p: Kāmarāgānusayassa pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati, paṭighānusayassa …pe…
segs.e: The underlying tendencies of sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sattannaṁ anusayānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: The spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these seven underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmarāgānusayo pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo.
segs.e: When a mendicant has given up the underlying tendencies of sensual desire, repulsion, views, doubt, conceit, desire to be reborn, and ignorance—cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they are unable to arise in the future—

segs.p: avijjānusayo pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo.
Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”ti.
segs.e: they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”
Numbered Discourses 7.13
2. Tendencies
A Family

segs.p: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā nālaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā nālaṁ upanisīdituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, visiting a family with seven factors is not worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is not worthwhile.
What seven?

segs.p: Na manāpena paccuṭṭhenti, na manāpena abhivādenti, na manāpena āsanaṁ denti, santamassa pariguhanti, bahukampi thokaṁ denti, paṇītampi lūkhaṁ denti, asakkaccaṁ denti no sakkaccaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t politely rise, bow, or offer a seat. They hide what they have. Even when they have much they give little. Even when they have fine things they give coarse things. They give carelessly, not carefully.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā nālaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā nālaṁ upanisīdituṁ.
segs.e: Visiting a family with these seven factors is not worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is not worthwhile.

segs.p: Sattahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā alaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā alaṁ upanisīdituṁ.
segs.e: Visiting a family with seven factors is worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is worthwhile.
What seven?

segs.p: Manāpena paccuṭṭhenti, manāpena abhivādenti, manāpena āsanaṁ denti, santamassa na pariguhanti, bahukampi bahukaṁ denti, paṇītampi paṇītaṁ denti, sakkaccaṁ denti no asakkaccaṁ.
segs.e: They politely rise, bow, and offer a seat. They don’t hide what they have. When they have much they give much. When they have refined things they give refined things. They give carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi aṅgehi samannāgataṁ kulaṁ anupagantvā vā alaṁ upagantuṁ, upagantvā vā alaṁ upanisīditun”ti.
segs.e: Visiting a family with these seven factors is worthwhile, or if you’ve already arrived, sitting down is worthwhile.”
Numbered Discourses 7.14
2. Tendencies
Individuals

segs.p: “Sattime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these seven individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
What seven?

segs.p: Ubhatobhāgavimutto, paññāvimutto, kāyasakkhī, diṭṭhippatto, saddhāvimutto, dhammānusārī, saddhānusārī.
segs.e: The one freed both ways, the one freed by wisdom, the direct witness, the one attained to view, the one freed by faith, the follower of teachings, and the follower by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the seven individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 7.15
2. Tendencies
A Simile With Water

segs.p: “Sattime, bhikkhave, udakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these seven individuals found in the world are like those in water.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sakiṁ nimuggo nimuggova hoti;
segs.e: One individual sinks under once and stays under.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā nimujjati;
segs.e: One individual rises up then sinks under.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā ṭhito hoti;
segs.e: One individual rises up then stays put.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā vipassati viloketi;
segs.e: One individual rises up then sees and discerns.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā patarati;
segs.e: One individual rises up then crosses over.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā patigādhappatto hoti;
segs.e: One individual rises up then finds a foothold.

segs.p: idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā tiṇṇo hoti pāraṅgato thale tiṭṭhati brāhmaṇo.
segs.e: One individual has risen up, crossed over, and gone to the far shore, a brahmin who stands on solid ground.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo sakiṁ nimuggo nimuggova hoti?
segs.e: And what kind of individual sinks under once and stays under?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo samannāgato hoti ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi.
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who has absolutely dark, unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sakiṁ nimuggo nimuggova hoti.
segs.e: This kind of individual sinks under once and stays under.
And what kind of individual rises up then sinks under?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: Tassa sā saddhā neva tiṭṭhati no vaḍḍhati hāyatiyeva, tassa sā hirī …pe…
segs.e: However their faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom don’t last or grow, but dwindle away.

segs.p: tassa sā paññā neva tiṭṭhati no vaḍḍhati hāyatiyeva.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā nimujjati.
segs.e: This kind of individual rises up then sinks under.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā ṭhito hoti?
segs.e: And what kind of individual rises up then stays put?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: Tassa sā saddhā neva hāyati no vaḍḍhati ṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: And their faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom lasts, neither dwindling nor growing.

segs.p: tassa sā paññā neva hāyati no vaḍḍhati ṭhitā hoti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: This kind of individual rises up then stays put.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā vipassati viloketi?
segs.e: And what kind of individual rises up then sees and discerns?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā vipassati viloketi.
segs.e: This kind of individual rises up then sees and discerns.
And what kind of individual rises up then crosses over?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: So tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, they’re a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā patarati.
segs.e: This kind of individual rises up then crosses over.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā patigādhappatto hoti?
segs.e: And what kind of individual rises up then finds a foothold?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā patigādhappatto hoti.
segs.e: This kind of individual rises up then finds a foothold.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā tiṇṇo hoti pāraṅgato thale tiṭṭhati brāhmaṇo.
segs.e: And what kind of individual has risen up, crossed over, and gone to the far shore, a brahmin who stands on solid ground?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjati sādhu saddhā kusalesu dhammesu, sādhu hirī …pe…
segs.e: It’s the kind of individual who, rising up, thinks: ‘It’s good to have faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

segs.p: So āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ummujjitvā tiṇṇo hoti pāraṅgato thale tiṭṭhati brāhmaṇo.
segs.e: This kind of individual has risen up, crossed over, and gone to the far shore, a brahmin who stands on solid ground.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta udakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These seven individuals found in the world are like those in water.”
Numbered Discourses 7.16
2. Tendencies
Observing Impermanence

segs.p: “Sattime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these seven individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: First, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions. They perceive impermanence and experience impermanence. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom.

segs.p: So āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo puggalo āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the first individual.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: Next, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions.

segs.p: Tassa apubbaṁ acarimaṁ āsavapariyādānañca hoti jīvitapariyādānañca.
segs.e: Their defilements and their life come to an end at exactly the same time.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo puggalo āhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the second individual.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: Next, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions.

segs.p: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished between one life and the next. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished upon landing. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished without extra effort. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished with extra effort. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, sattamo puggalo āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the seventh individual.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the seven individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 7.17
2. Tendencies
Observing Suffering

segs.p: Sattime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these seven individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu dukkhānupassī viharati …pe….
segs.e: First, take an individual who meditates observing suffering in all conditions. They perceive suffering and experience suffering. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom. …”
Numbered Discourses 7.18
2. Tendencies
Observing Not-self

“First, take an individual who meditates observing not-self in all things. They perceive not-self and experience not-self. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom. …”
Numbered Discourses 7.19
2. Tendencies
Extinguishment

segs.p: “Nibbāne sukhānupassī viharati sukhasaññī sukhapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: “One meditates observing the happiness in extinguishment. They perceive happiness and experience happiness. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom.

segs.p: So āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ayaṁ bhikkhave, paṭhamo puggalo āhuneyyo …pe… puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the first individual worthy of offerings.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo nibbāne sukhānupassī viharati sukhasaññī sukhapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: Next, take an individual who meditates observing the happiness in extinguishment. They perceive happiness and experience happiness. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom.

segs.p: Tassa apubbaṁ acarimaṁ āsavapariyādānañca hoti jīvitapariyādānañca.
segs.e: Their defilements and their life come to an end at exactly the same time.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo puggalo āhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the second individual.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo nibbāne sukhānupassī viharati sukhasaññī sukhapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
segs.e: Next, take an individual who meditates observing the happiness in extinguishment. They perceive happiness and experience happiness. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom.

segs.p: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished between one life and the next. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished upon landing. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished without extra effort. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished with extra effort. …
With the ending of the five lower fetters they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, sattamo puggalo āhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: This is the seventh individual.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the seven individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 7.20
2. Tendencies
Qualifications for Graduation
“Mendicants, there are these seven qualifications for graduation.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca sikkhāsamādāne avigatapemo,
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

segs.p: dhammanisantiyā tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca dhammanisantiyā avigatapemo,
segs.e: to examine the teachings …

segs.p: icchāvinaye tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca icchāvinaye avigatapemo,
segs.e: to get rid of desires …

segs.p: paṭisallāne tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca paṭisallāne avigatapemo,
segs.e: for retreat …

segs.p: vīriyārambhe tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca vīriyārambhe avigatapemo,
segs.e: to rouse up energy …

segs.p: satinepakke tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca satinepakke avigatapemo,
segs.e: for mindfulness and alertness …

segs.p: diṭṭhipaṭivedhe tibbacchando hoti āyatiñca diṭṭhipaṭivedhe avigatapemo.
segs.e: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.
These are the seven qualifications for graduation.”
Numbered Discourses 7.21
3. The Vajji Seven
At Sārandada
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati sārandade cetiye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Sārandada Shrine.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā licchavī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te licchavī bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then several Licchavis went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and the Buddha said to these Licchavis:
“Licchavis, I will teach you these seven principles that prevent decline.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te licchavī bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī abhiṇhaṁ sannipātā bhavissanti sannipātabahulā;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis meet frequently and have many meetings,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karissanti;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis meet in harmony, leave in harmony, and carry on their business in harmony,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī apaññattaṁ na paññāpessanti, paññattaṁ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattissanti;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis don’t make new decrees or abolish existing decrees, but proceed having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they have been decreed,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī ye te vajjīnaṁ vajjimahallakā te sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṁ maññissanti;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate Vajjian elders, and think them worth listening to,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okassa pasayha vāsessanti;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis don’t forcibly abduct the women or girls of the clans and make them live with them,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṁ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca tāni sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ dhammikaṁ baliṁ no parihāpessanti;
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian shrines, whether inner or outer, not neglecting the proper spirit-offerings that were given and made in the past,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṁvihitā bhavissati:
segs.e: As long as the Vajjis organize proper protection, shelter, and security for perfected ones, so that

segs.p: ‘kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṁ āgaccheyyuṁ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsuṁ vihareyyun’ti;
segs.e: more perfected ones might come to the realm and those already here may live in comfort,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, licchavī, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā vajjīsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu vajjī sandississanti;
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the Vajjis, and as long as the Vajjis are seen following them,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, licchavī, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.22
3. The Vajji Seven
With Vassakāra
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, wanted to invade the Vajjis.
He said:

segs.p: “ahaṁ hime vajjī evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi, vajjī vināsessāmi, vajjī anayabyasanaṁ āpādessāmī”ti.
segs.e: “I shall wipe out these Vajjis, so mighty and powerful! I shall destroy them, and lay ruin and devastation upon them!”

segs.p: Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vassakāraṁ brāhmaṇaṁ māgadhamahāmattaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: And then King Ajātasattu addressed Vassakāra the brahmin, a chief minister of Magadha,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ puccha:
segs.e: “Please, brahmin, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Ask him if he is healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

segs.p: ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ pucchatī’ti.

segs.e: And then say:

segs.p: ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo.
segs.e: ‘Sir, King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, wants to invade the Vajjis.
He said:

segs.p: ahaṁ hime vajjī evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi, vajjī vināsessāmi, vajjī anayabyasanaṁ āpādessāmī’ti.
segs.e: “I shall wipe out these Vajjis, so mighty and powerful! I shall destroy them, and lay ruin and devastation upon them!”’

segs.p: Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti, taṁ sādhukaṁ uggahetvā mama āroceyyāsi.
segs.e: Remember well how the Buddha answers and tell it to me.
For Realized Ones say nothing that is not so.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo māgadhamahāmatto rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” Vassakāra replied. He went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo māgadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “rājā, bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṁ appātaṅkaṁ lahuṭṭhānaṁ balaṁ phāsuvihāraṁ pucchati.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, King Ajātasattu bows with his head to your feet. He asks if you are healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

segs.p: Rājā, bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo.
segs.e: King Ajātasattu wants to invade the Vajjis.
He said:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ hime vajjī evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi, vajjī vināsessāmi, vajjī anayabyasanaṁ āpādessāmī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I shall wipe out these Vajjis, so mighty and powerful! I shall destroy them, and lay ruin and devastation upon them!’”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando bhagavato piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṁ bījayamāno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Ānanda was standing behind the Buddha fanning him.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī abhiṇhaṁ sannipātā sannipātabahulā’”ti?
segs.e: “Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis meet frequently and have many meetings?”
“I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī abhiṇhaṁ sannipātā bhavissanti sannipātabahulā; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis meet frequently and have many meetings, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis meet in harmony, leave in harmony, and carry on their business in harmony?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karissanti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis meet in harmony, leave in harmony, and carry on their business in harmony, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī apaññattaṁ na paññāpenti, paññattaṁ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis don’t make new decrees or abolish existing decrees, but proceed having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they have been decreed?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjī apaññattaṁ na paññāpenti, paññattaṁ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī apaññattaṁ na paññāpessanti, paññattaṁ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattissanti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis don’t make new decrees or abolish existing decrees, but proceed having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they have been decreed, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī ye te vajjīnaṁ vajjimahallakā te sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṁ maññantī’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate Vajjian elders, and think them worth listening to?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjī ye te vajjīnaṁ vajjimahallakā te sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṁ maññantī’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī ye te vajjīnaṁ vajjimahallakā te sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṁ maññissanti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate Vajjian elders, and think them worth listening to, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okassa pasayha vāsentī’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis don’t forcibly abduct the women or girls of the clans and make them live with them?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okassa pasayha vāsentī’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okassa pasayha vāsessanti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis don’t forcibly abduct the women or girls of the clans and make them live with them, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṁ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca tāni sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ dhammikaṁ baliṁ no parihāpentī’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian shrines, whether inner or outer, not neglecting the proper spirit-offerings that were given and made in the past?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṁ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca tāni sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ dhammikaṁ baliṁ no parihāpentī’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṁ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca tāni sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ dhammikaṁ baliṁ no parihāpessanti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian shrines, whether inner or outer, not neglecting the proper spirit-offerings that were given and made in the past, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṁ: ‘vajjīnaṁ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṁvihitā—kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṁ āgaccheyyuṁ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsuṁ vihareyyun’”ti?
segs.e: Ānanda, have you heard that the Vajjis organize proper protection, shelter, and security for perfected ones, so that more perfected ones might come to the realm and those already here may live in comfort?”

segs.p: “Sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante: ‘vajjīnaṁ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṁvihitā bhavissati—kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṁ āgaccheyyuṁ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsuṁ vihareyyun’”ti.
segs.e: “I have heard that, sir.”

segs.p: “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṁvihitā bhavissati: ‘kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṁ āgaccheyyuṁ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsuṁ vihareyyun’ti; vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: “As long as the Vajjis organize proper protection, shelter, and security for perfected ones, so that more perfected ones might come to the realm and those already here may live in comfort, they can expect growth, not decline.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā vassakāraṁ brāhmaṇaṁ māgadhamahāmattaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Vassakāra:

segs.p: “ekamidāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, samayaṁ vesāliyaṁ viharāmi sārandade cetiye.
segs.e: “Brahmin, this one time I was staying near Vesālī at the Sārandada Shrine.

segs.p: Tatrāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vajjīnaṁ ime satta aparihāniye dhamme desesiṁ.
segs.e: There I taught the Vajjis these principles that prevent decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, brāhmaṇa, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā vajjīsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu vajjī sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, brāhmaṇa, vajjīnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the Vajjis, and as long as the Vajjis are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”

segs.p: “Ekamekenapi, bho gotama, aparihāniyena dhammena samannāgatānaṁ vajjīnaṁ vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni;
segs.e: When the Buddha had spoken, Vassakāra said to him: “Worthy Gotama, if the Vajjis follow even a single one of these principles they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: ko pana vādo sattahi aparihāniyehi dhammehi.
segs.e: How much more so all seven!

segs.p: Akaraṇīyā ca, bho gotama, vajjī raññā māgadhena ajātasattunā vedehiputtena yadidaṁ yuddhassa, aññatra upalāpanāya, aññatra mithubhedā.
segs.e: King Ajātasattu cannot defeat the Vajjis in war, unless by bribery or by sowing dissension.

segs.p: Handa ca dāni mayaṁ, bho gotama, gacchāma, bahukiccā mayaṁ bahukaraṇīyā”ti.
segs.e: Well, now, worthy Gotama, I must go. I have many duties, and much to do.”
“Please, brahmin, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo māgadhamahāmatto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then Vassakāra the brahmin, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, rose from his seat and left.
Numbered Discourses 7.23
3. The Vajji Seven
Non-Decline for Mendicants (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:
“Mendicants, I will teach you these seven principles that prevent decline.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiṇhaṁ sannipātā bhavissanti sannipātabahulā; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants meet frequently and have many meetings, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā saṅghakaraṇīyāni karissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants meet in harmony, leave in harmony, and carry on their business in harmony, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū apaññattaṁ na paññāpessanti, paññattaṁ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants don’t make new decrees or abolish existing decrees, but proceed having undertaken the training rules as they have been decreed, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṁ maññissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the senior mendicants—of long standing, long gone forth, fathers and leaders of the Saṅgha—and think them worth listening to, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū uppannāya taṇhāya ponobhavikāya na vasaṁ gacchissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants don’t fall under the sway of arisen craving for future lives, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū āraññakesu senāsanesu sāpekkhā bhavissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants take care to live in wilderness lodgings, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū paccattaññeva satiṁ upaṭṭhāpessanti: ‘kinti anāgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī āgaccheyyuṁ, āgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī phāsuṁ vihareyyun’ti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants individually establish mindfulness, so that more good-hearted spiritual companions might come, and those that have already come may live comfortably, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the mendicants, and as long as the mendicants are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.24
3. The Vajji Seven
Non-Decline for Mendicants (2nd)
“Mendicants, I will teach you seven principles that prevent decline.
Listen and apply your mind well …

segs.p: katame ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na kammārāmā bhavissanti, na kammaratā, na kammārāmataṁ anuyuttā; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants don’t relish work, loving it and liking to relish it, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na bhassārāmā bhavissanti …pe…
segs.e: As long as they don’t enjoy talk …
sleep …
company …

segs.p: na pāpicchā bhavissanti na pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā …
segs.e: they don’t have corrupt wishes, falling under the sway of corrupt wishes …

segs.p: na pāpamittā bhavissanti na pāpasahāyā na pāpasampavaṅkā …
segs.e: they don’t have bad friends, companions, and associates …

segs.p: na oramattakena visesādhigamena antarāvosānaṁ āpajjissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: they don’t stop half-way after achieving some trifling distinction, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the mendicants, and as long as the mendicants are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.25
3. The Vajji Seven
Non-Decline for Mendicants (3rd)
“Mendicants, I will teach you seven principles that prevent decline.
Listen and apply your mind well …

segs.p: katame ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū saddhā bhavissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants are faithful …
conscientious …
prudent …
learned …
energetic …
mindful …

segs.p: paññavanto bhavissanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: wise, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the mendicants, and as long as the mendicants are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.26
3. The Vajji Seven
Awakening Factors
“Mendicants, I will teach you seven principles that prevent decline.
Listen and apply your mind well …

segs.p: katame ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāvessanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants develop the awakening factor of mindfulness …
investigation of principles …
energy …
rapture …
tranquility …
immersion …

segs.p: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāvessanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: equanimity, they can expect growth, not decline.

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the mendicants, and as long as the mendicants are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.27
3. The Vajji Seven
Perceptions
“Mendicants, I will teach you seven principles that prevent decline.
Listen and apply your mind well …

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā?
segs.e: And what are the seven principles that prevent decline?

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aniccasaññaṁ bhāvessanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.
segs.e: As long as the mendicants develop the perception of impermanence …
not-self …
ugliness …
drawbacks …
giving up …
fading away …
cessation,

segs.p: vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni. Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu, bhikkhū sandississanti; vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṁ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.
segs.e: they can expect growth, not decline. As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the mendicants, and as long as the mendicants are seen following them, they can expect growth, not decline.”
Numbered Discourses 7.28
3. The Vajji Seven
Non-decline for a Mendicant Trainee
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “sattime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These seven things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What seven?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, saṅgaṇikārāmatā, indriyesu aguttadvāratā, bhojane amattaññutā, santi kho pana saṅghe saṅghakaraṇīyāni; tatra sekho bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: They relish work, talk, sleep, and company. They don’t guard the sense doors and they eat too much. And when there is Saṅgha business to be carried out, they don’t reflect:

segs.p: ‘santi kho pana saṅghe therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā bhāravāhino, te tena paññāyissantī’ti attanā tesu yogaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: ‘There are senior mendicants in the Saṅgha of long standing, long gone forth, responsible. They’ll be known for taking care of this.’ So they get involved in that.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These seven things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Sattime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What seven?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, na saṅgaṇikārāmatā, indriyesu guttadvāratā, bhojane mattaññutā, santi kho pana saṅghe saṅghakaraṇīyāni; tatra sekho bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: They don’t relish work, talk, sleep, and company. They guard the sense doors and don’t eat too much. And when there is Saṅgha business to be carried out, they reflect:

segs.p: ‘santi kho pana saṅghe therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā bhāravāhino, te tena paññāyissantī’ti attanā na tesu yogaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: ‘There are senior mendicants in the Saṅgha of long standing, long gone forth, responsible. They’ll be known for taking care of this.’ So they don’t get involved in that.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”
Numbered Discourses 7.29
3. The Vajji Seven
Non-decline for a Lay Follower
“These seven things lead to the decline of a lay follower.
What seven?
They miss out on seeing the mendicants.
They neglect listening to the true teaching.
They don’t train in higher ethical conduct.
They’re very suspicious about mendicants, whether senior, junior, or middle.

segs.p: bhikkhūsu theresu ceva navesu ca majjhimesu ca upārambhacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti randhagavesī,
segs.e: They listen to the teaching with a hostile, fault-finding mind.
They seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.
And they serve them first.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta dhammā upāsakassa parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These seven things lead to the decline of a lay follower.

segs.p: Sattime, bhikkhave, dhammā upāsakassa aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a lay follower.
What seven?
They don’t miss out on seeing the mendicants.
They don’t neglect listening to the true teaching.
They train in higher ethical conduct.
They’re very confident about mendicants, whether senior, junior, or middle.

segs.p: bhikkhūsu theresu ceva navesu ca majjhimesu ca anupārambhacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti na randhagavesī,
segs.e: They don’t listen to the teaching with a hostile, fault-finding mind.
They don’t seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.
And they serve the Buddhist community first.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta dhammā upāsakassa aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a lay follower.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“A lay follower misses out on seeing
those who are evolved
and listening to the teachings of the Noble One.
They don’t train in higher ethical conduct,
and their suspicion about mendicants
just grows and grows.
They want to listen to the true teaching
with a fault-finding mind.
They seek outside the Buddhist community
for someone else worthy of religious donations,
and that lay follower
serves them first.
These seven principles leading to decline
have been well taught.
A lay follower who practices them
falls away from the true teaching.
A lay follower doesn’t miss out on seeing
those who are evolved
and listening to the teachings of the Noble One.
They train in higher ethical conduct,
and their confidence in mendicants
just grows and grows.
They want to listen to the true teaching
without a fault-finding mind.
They don’t seek outside the Buddhist community
for someone else worthy of religious donations,
and that lay follower
serves the Buddhist community first.
These seven principles that prevent decline
have been well taught.
A lay follower who practices them
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 7.30
3. The Vajji Seven
Failures for a Lay Follower
“Mendicants, there are these seven failures for a lay follower …
There are these seven accomplishments for a lay follower …”
Numbered Discourses 7.31
3. The Vajji Seven
Downfalls for a Lay Follower
“Mendicants, there are these seven downfalls for a lay follower …
There are these seven successes for a lay follower.
What seven?
They don’t miss out on seeing the mendicants.
They don’t neglect listening to the true teaching.
They train in higher ethical conduct.
They’re very confident about mendicants, whether senior, junior, or middle.

segs.p: bhikkhūsu theresu ceva navesu ca majjhimesu ca anupārambhacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti na randhagavesī,
segs.e: They don’t listen to the teaching with a hostile, fault-finding mind.
They don’t seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.
And they serve the Buddhist community first.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta upāsakassa sambhavāti.
segs.e: These are the seven successes for a lay follower.
A lay follower misses out on seeing
those who are evolved
and listening to the teachings of the Noble One.
They don’t train in higher ethical conduct,
and their suspicion about mendicants
just grows and grows.
They want to listen to the true teaching
with a fault-finding mind.
They seek outside the Buddhist community
for someone else worthy of religious donations,
and that lay follower
serves them first.
These seven principles leading to decline
have been well taught.
A lay follower who practices these
falls away from the true teaching.
A lay follower doesn’t miss out on seeing
those who are evolved
and listening to the teachings of the Noble One.
They train in higher ethical conduct,
and their confidence in mendicants
just grows and grows.
They want to listen to the true teaching
without a fault-finding mind.
They don’t seek outside the Buddhist community
for someone else worthy of religious donations,
and that lay follower
serves the Buddhist community first.
These seven principles that prevent decline
have been well taught.
A lay follower who practices them
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 7.32
4. Deities
Respect for Diligence

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, these seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.
What seven?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, samādhigāravatā, appamādagāravatā, paṭisanthāragāravatā.
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for immersion, for diligence, and for hospitality.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante, satta dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.”
That is what that deity said,
and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho sā devatā “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened, adding:

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, samādhigāravatā, appamādagāravatā, paṭisanthāragāravatā—
ime kho, bhante, satta dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

segs.e: “Respect for the Teacher and the teaching,
and keen respect for the Saṅgha;
respect for immersion, being energetic,
and keen respect for the training.
A mendicant who respects diligence
and hospitality
can’t decline,
and has drawn near to extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 7.33
4. Deities
Respect for Conscience

segs.p: “Imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:
‘Sir, these seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.
What seven?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, samādhigāravatā, hirigāravatā, ottappagāravatā.
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for immersion, for conscience, and for prudence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante, satta dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’
That is what that deity said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.
One respectful of the Teacher and the teaching,
keenly respecting the Saṅgha;
respecting immersion, being energetic,
and keenly respecting the training;
endowed with conscience and prudence,
reverential and respectful—
it is impossible for them to decline;
they have drawn near to extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 7.34
4. Deities
Easy to Admonish (1st)

segs.p: “Imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā …pe… maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight a deity … said to me:
‘Sir, these seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.
What seven?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, samādhigāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā.
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for immersion; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante, satta dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’
That is what that deity said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.
Respect for the Teacher and the teaching,
and keen respect for the Saṅgha;
respecting immersion, being energetic,
and keen respect for the training.
One with good friends, easy to admonish,
reverential and respectful,
can’t decline,
and has drawn near to extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 7.35
4. Deities
Easy to Admonish (2nd)

segs.p: “Imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, tonight a deity … said to me:
‘Sir, these seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.
What seven?

segs.p: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, samādhigāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā.
segs.e: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training, for immersion; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante, satta dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
segs.e: These seven things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’
That is what that deity said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, this is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.

segs.p: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti, satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher and praises such respect.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack such respect to respect the Teacher.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who respect the Teacher at the right time, truthfully and correctly.
They personally respect the teaching …
They personally respect the Saṅgha …
They personally respect the training …
They personally respect immersion …
They are personally easy to admonish …
They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālenāti.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”
“Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, sāriputta, imassa mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi.
segs.e: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti, satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher …

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack such respect to respect the Teacher.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who respect the Teacher at the right time, truthfully and correctly.
They personally respect the teaching …
They personally respect the Saṅgha …
They personally respect the training …
They personally respect immersion …
They are personally easy to admonish …
They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
segs.e: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

segs.p: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālenāti.
segs.e: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Imassa kho, sāriputta, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
segs.e: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”
Numbered Discourses 7.36
4. Deities
A Friend (1st)
“Mendicants, you should associate with a friend who has seven factors.
What seven?

segs.p: Duddadaṁ dadāti, dukkaraṁ karoti, dukkhamaṁ khamati, guyhamassa āvi karoti, guyhamassa pariguhati, āpadāsu na jahati, khīṇena nātimaññati.
segs.e: They give what is hard to give. They do what is hard to do. They endure what is hard to endure. They reveal their secrets to you. They keep your secrets. They don’t abandon you in times of trouble. They don’t look down on you in times of loss.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi aṅgehi samannāgato mitto sevitabboti.
segs.e: You should associate with a friend who has these seven factors.
A friend gives what is hard to give,
and does what’s hard to do.
They put up with your harsh words,
and with things hard to endure.
They tell you their secrets,
and keep your secrets for you.
They don’t abandon you in times of trouble,
or look down on you in times of loss.
The individual in whom
these things are found is your friend.
If you want to have a friend,
you should keep company with that sort.”
Numbered Discourses 7.37
4. Deities
A Friend (2nd)

segs.p: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo api panujjamānenapi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a friend has seven qualities you should associate with, accompany, and attend them, even if they drive you away.
What seven?

segs.p: Piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca vattā ca vacanakkhamo ca gambhīrañca kathaṁ kattā hoti, no ca aṭṭhāne niyojeti.
segs.e: They’re liked, agreeable, respected, and admired. They admonish you and they accept admonishment. They speak on deep matters. And they don’t urge you to do bad things.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, sattahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo api panujjamānenapīti.
segs.e: When a friend has these seven qualities you should associate with, accompany, and attend them, even if they drive you away.
They’re liked, respected, and admired,
an admonisher who accepts admonishment,
speaks on deep matters,
and doesn’t urge you to do bad.
The individual in whom
these things are found is your friend.
If you want to have a friend,
benevolent and sympathetic,
then even if they chase you away,
you should keep company with that sort.”
Numbered Discourses 7.38
4. Deities
Textual Analysis (1st)

segs.p: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva catasso paṭisambhidā sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with seven qualities will soon realize the four kinds of textual analysis and live having achieved them with their own insight.
What seven?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ me cetaso līnattan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is mental sluggishness’.

segs.p: ajjhattaṁ saṅkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ ‘ajjhattaṁ me saṅkhittaṁ cittan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti;
